text: The anti-discrimination measure refiled in the Senate in July 2025 for the 20th Congress is known as the SOGIESC Equality Bill. What does SOGIESC stand for?
optionA: Sexual Orientation, Gender Identity or Expression, and Sex Characteristics
optionB: Social Orientation, Gender Inclusion and Equal Social Care
optionC: Sexual Orientation, Gender Identity, Equality and Social Conduct
optionD: Sex, Orientation, Gender Inclusion, Equity and Social Citizenship

text: As of November 2026, which statement best describes the status of the SOGIE (SOGIESC) Equality Bill?
optionA: It was signed into law in 2024 as the SOGIESC Equality Act.
optionB: It was refiled in the 20th Congress and has not yet been enacted into law.
optionC: It was vetoed by the President after both chambers approved it in 2025.
optionD: It was declared unconstitutional by the Supreme Court in 2023.

text: On September 20, 2017, the House of Representatives approved the SOGIE Equality Bill (House Bill 4982) on third and final reading. What happened to that measure afterward?
optionA: It was signed into law within 30 days of its transmittal.
optionB: It lapsed into law without the President's signature.
optionC: It was submitted to the people in a national referendum.
optionD: The Senate did not pass it before the 17th Congress ended, so it did not become law.

text: The SOGIESC Equality Bill, refiled in the 20th Congress in July 2025, is an anti-discrimination measure. Which act does it propose to treat as discriminatory?
optionA: Requiring all employees to undergo annual drug testing
optionB: Charging higher tuition to foreign students
optionC: Refusing to admit or expelling a student from a school because of his or her SOGIESC
optionD: Requiring government employees to wear a uniform

text: In April 2026, the Philippines signed on to the Pax Silica declaration. What is Pax Silica?
optionA: A United States-led coalition of countries aiming to build secure supply chains for semiconductors and artificial intelligence technology
optionB: A China-led maritime infrastructure program under the Belt and Road Initiative
optionC: An ASEAN code of conduct on the South China Sea
optionD: A United Nations treaty banning the export of raw silica sand

text: After the Philippines joined the US-led Pax Silica initiative in April 2026, the Bases Conversion and Development Authority (BCDA) identified which site to host a planned AI industrial hub?
Executive Order No. 94, signed on September 11, 2025, created which body to investigate anomalies in flood control and other infrastructure projects?
In August 2025, Malacañang launched a website where the public could view government flood control projects on a map and report complaints or feedback. What is it called?

The Senate Blue Ribbon Committee and the Independent Commission for Infrastructure (ICI) both looked into flood control anomalies in 2025. Which office files the resulting criminal cases before the Sandiganbayan?

The House of Representatives impeached Vice President Sara Duterte on May 11, 2026. Under Article XI, Section 3(6) of the 1987 Constitution, which body has the sole power to try and decide all cases of impeachment?

On February 5, 2025, more than one-third of all the Members of the House signed a verified impeachment complaint against Vice President Sara Duterte. Under Article XI, Section 3(4) of the 1987 Constitution, what is the effect of a complaint filed by at least one-third of all the Members of the House?
optionA: It must first be heard by the House Committee on Justice within 60 session days.
optionB: It must first be reviewed by the Supreme Court before it can be sent to the Senate.
optionC: It must be approved by a majority of the Senate before a trial can begin.
optionD: It constitutes the Articles of Impeachment, and trial by the Senate shall forthwith proceed.

text: The Senate convened as an impeachment court on May 18, 2026 to try Vice President Sara Duterte. Under Article XI, Section 3(6) of the 1987 Constitution, what vote is required to convict?
optionA: Concurrence of two-thirds of all the Members of the Senate
optionB: Majority of the Senators present, provided there is a quorum
optionC: One-third of all the Members of the Senate
optionD: Unanimous vote of all the Senators

text: In July 2025, the Supreme Court unanimously declared void the Articles of Impeachment transmitted to the Senate in February 2025 against Vice President Sara Duterte, and it denied the House's motion for reconsideration in January 2026. The ruling rested mainly on which constitutional rule?
optionA: The two-thirds Senate vote required for conviction
optionB: The bar against initiating impeachment proceedings against the same official more than once within one year
optionC: The rule that the Chief Justice presides when the President is on trial
optionD: The rule limiting judgment to removal and disqualification from office

text: After the Supreme Court declared the 2025 Articles of Impeachment against Vice President Sara Duterte void, what did the Senate do with those articles on August 6, 2025?
optionA: It voted to acquit the Vice President on all articles.
optionB: It referred the articles to the Office of the Ombudsman for prosecution.
optionC: It voted to archive the articles of impeachment.
optionD: It forwarded the articles to the Supreme Court for trial.

text: As of November 2026, the Senate sitting as an impeachment court is hearing the case against Vice President Sara Duterte. Under Article XI, Section 3(7) of the 1987 Constitution, judgment in impeachment cases shall not extend further than:
optionA: imprisonment and a fine set by the Senate
optionB: removal from office and disqualification to hold any office under the Republic
optionC: forfeiture of all properties in favor of the State
optionD: suspension from office for one year without pay
